originality.rationale: The main recent paper (arXiv:2605.03664, Sections 3 and 4) derives the waiting PGF and flags autocorrelation for future research, but contains no renewal-arrival Hausdorff mixing law or corresponding fixed-lag covariance limit. Pachon–Polito–Ricciuti analyze discrete semi-Markov counts/time changes, not these renewal arrival indicators; Ferreira develops general complete monotonicity for related fractional Volterra equations without stating this model-specific spectral density and its aging covariance. Classical renewal regeneration explains one proof ingredient, not the whole result. Existing results in different terminology could still subsume parts of the claim.
residual_risks: The general Volterra complete-monotonicity theorem might imply the mixture formula by a nontrivial reduction not recognized here.
Additional historical renewal-correlation results not found by the searches could directly cover the asymptotic aging profile.

value.rationale: The explicit positive mixing density enforces strict complete monotonicity and all-time positive renewal-indicator dependence; the nonstationary aging correlation tends to a nonsummable power-law profile. It answers a well-motivated dependence question for the discrete fractional renewal law while distinguishing it carefully from stationary long-range dependence.
